summary: Wooden cab on a stone base atop Yellow Mountain, Nantahala NF, Macon County, NC; trail guides date it to 1934 (CCC); NHLR-registered 1992; restored; reached on foot.

facts.design: Wooden cab about 14 by 14 ft with a steep pyramid roof on an 8-ft stone base

access.note: On Nantahala National Forest land and reached by a hiking trail; trail guides describe it as a hiking destination. No source states current rules for climbing the cabin itself.

visit.trail_note: Hike on the Yellow Mountain Trail from Buck Creek Road near Highlands. Guides name different starting gaps (Cody Gap, Cole Gap).

events.note: Trail guides date the build to 1934; one credits the Civilian Conservation Corps
One trail guide says the cabin was staffed until 1969 (single secondary source)
Registered June 1, 1992 as US 42, NC 1; nominated by Dave Cawrse, District Ranger, USFS Highlands Ranger District
NHLR text says the cabin has been restored by volunteers and Highlands Ranger District staff; no restoration date given. A trail guide dated 26 January 2021 calls it recently restored.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two trail guides name different starting gaps on Buck Creek Road: Cody Gap (Bike/Hike Trails) and Cole Gap (sweetwilder). The story does not name a gap and tells visitors to check a current map.
Both trail guides give 1934 as the build year. Only one credits the CCC and the Register does not give a build date, so the credit is attributed to that guide alone.

notes_for_editor: Only the NHLR page is an official record. Build year and the 1969 staffing end come from two hiking-guide sites, not from Forest Service or archive records. A Transylvania Times destination-hike article (1934 build, USFS and CCC) returned HTTP 429 twice, so it is not used. Another guide snippet (theoutdoorsapp) mentions the tower was 'originally in 1934' and 'reconstru...' (cut off). If the tower was rebuilt, the built and restored events need correcting, so check the Forest Service or NRHP records before publishing. The record has no height; the NHLR gives only the cab and base dimensions, so height_m was left out. Access is marked public on the basis of trail access on national forest land; confirm current climbing rules with the Highlands Ranger District.
